families.title: Appropriations
families.mechanism: Provides money for a program that is already authorized, up to what that authority allows.

structuralProvenance.establishes: An official estimate distinguishes authorizing legislation from appropriation treatment and states which effects it did not model, rather than presenting one confident total.

evidence.note: An authored standing program. No real transit fund, statute or appropriation is described, and its ceiling is a design choice rather than a figure read from anywhere.

standingAuthorities.citationLabel: the School Facilities Revolving Fund Act

evidence.note: An authored standing program. The game asserts no real school construction fund and no real balance in one.
An authored standing duty with no money attached. No real records statute is described.

intendedOutcome.statement: How much of what was provided is actually obligated and spent, and when.

evidence.note: Money provided is not money spent, and the schedule on which it goes out is its own question.
evidence.unavailableReason: An appropriation alone records no commitment or payment. Before an office commits funds and an installment is paid, no outlay can be reported from the bill itself.

variants.label: Appropriation to a single program
variants.synopsis: Provides money for one program that is already authorized. It creates no program and widens no eligibility.
declaredLimits: It provides money. It does not change who qualifies, what the program does, or how long it runs.
It cannot provide more than the authority it names allows.
Money provided is not money spent. The governing office must commit it, and a payment must clear before an outlay is recorded.

evidence.note: An authored range. Its upper end deliberately exceeds what some authorities allow, so a bill that would overspend its authority is refused rather than quietly reduced.
An authored availability period. Real lapse rules vary by state and none is reproduced here.

options.label: An annual statement of what was spent
options.clausePhrase: an annual statement of the amounts obligated and expended under this appropriation

options.label: A quarterly statement of what was spent
options.clausePhrase: a quarterly statement of the amounts obligated and expended under this appropriation

options.label: Quarterly, and what remains unobligated
options.clausePhrase: a quarterly statement of the amounts obligated and expended under this appropriation and of the amount that remains unobligated

evidence.note: An authored reporting duty. No real reporting statute is reproduced.

amendmentInvitation.heading: Set-aside for the counties with the oldest awards
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: counties that have waited longest for an award
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the counties at the back of the queue
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: The same counties have been at the back of this queue every year the fund has existed, and an appropriation with no set-aside will put them there again.

evidence.reference: Senate Amendment 2638 to Senate Amendment 2137, 117th Congress
evidence.establishes: A narrow targeted section can be drafted, sponsored and laid on the table without ever entering the enacted text, so proposed text and adopted text are different records.

amendmentInvitation.text: Of the amount appropriated by this Act, not less than {{amount-label}} shall be reserved for applicants whose applications have been pending longest, and any part of that reservation not awarded within the period of availability shall be released.

variants.label: Supplemental appropriation
variants.synopsis: Provides money mid-year for an authority already running, on a short availability with a hard lapse.
declaredLimits: It is a top-up. It provides money and changes nothing else about the program.
Its availability is short by design, and what is not obligated lapses.

evidence.note: An authored range for a mid-year top-up. It is smaller than a full-year appropriation because that is the design, not because anything measured says so.
An authored short availability. No real lapse rule is reproduced.

options.label: A statement when the money lapses
options.clausePhrase: a statement, within thirty days after the appropriation lapses, of the amount that lapsed and why

options.label: A statement when the money is committed
options.clausePhrase: a statement, within thirty days after the full amount is obligated, identifying each award made from it

evidence.note: An authored reporting duty.

rendering.text: This Act makes a supplemental appropriation for {{authority:programLabel}} as authorized by {{authority:citationLabel}}. It is supplemental to, and not in substitution for, any amount already provided for that purpose.

amendmentInvitation.heading: Carryforward for awards already in progress
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: applicants whose awards straddle the lapse date
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the projects that will be halfway through when it lapses
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A hard lapse date falls in the middle of work that is already under way, and the money goes back rather than finishing it.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. Nothing in the world says it was granted.

amendmentInvitation.text: Notwithstanding the lapse required by this Act, not more than {{amount-label}} obligated for work commenced before the lapse date shall remain available until that work is complete.

variants.label: Appropriation conditioned on a local match
variants.synopsis: Provides money only to the extent a local government puts up a stated share of its own.
declaredLimits: A local government that cannot raise the match draws nothing, however much is appropriated.
The match requirement is a condition on the money, not a change to who is eligible under the program itself.

evidence.note: An authored range for a matched appropriation.
An authored match share. Real match requirements vary widely and none is reproduced; zero is offered because a match of nothing is a real legislative choice.
An authored availability period, longer than a supplemental because raising a match takes a budget cycle.

rendering.text: The appropriation made by this Act is for {{authority:programLabel}} as authorized by {{authority:citationLabel}}, and is subject to the condition stated in this Act.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone {{authority:citationLabel}} already reaches

requiredAuthority.message: A matched appropriation reached its authority clause without an authority.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: the program named in Section 1

rendering.text: No amount appropriated by this Act shall be disbursed to a local government except to the extent that the local government commits, from its own funds, an amount equal to {{integer:match-share}} per cent of the amount disbursed. A local government that commits less receives proportionately less, and receives nothing if it commits nothing.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every local government able to commit the required share

rendering.text: No local contribution is required as a condition of disbursement under this Act.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every local government within the period

amendmentInvitation.heading: Waiver of the match for the least able to pay
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: local governments that cannot raise the match
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the counties whose whole road budget is smaller than the match
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A match requirement gives the money to the places that already had some, and the places that need it most are the ones that will not draw a dollar.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It is the ask that would turn a matched appropriation into a partly unmatched one.

amendmentInvitation.text: Not more than {{amount-label}} of the amount appropriated by this Act may be disbursed without regard to the condition in Section 3, to local governments demonstrating that the required share exceeds their capacity to raise it.

families.title: Sunset and repeal
families.mechanism: Ends, shortens or extends an authority that already exists, without providing or withdrawing a dollar.

structuralProvenance.establishes: An official estimate distinguishes authorizing legislation from appropriation treatment and states which effects it did not model, rather than presenting one confident total.

intendedOutcome.statement: Which authorities are in force, and what changes for the people who relied on one that ends.

evidence.note: Repealing an authority removes a ceiling. What that does to anyone depends on what was being spent under it, which is a different question.
evidence.unavailableReason: Nothing in this world records what has been spent under a standing authority, so the effect of ending one cannot be reported.

variants.label: Sunset on a stated date
variants.synopsis: Sets a date after which an existing authority has no further effect, with a report due before it arrives.
declaredLimits: It states no amount and provides no money. Removing a ceiling is not a saving anybody has banked.
It does not recover money already provided under the authority it ends.

evidence.note: An authored sunset horizon. No real sunset schedule is reproduced.

parameters.label: What must happen before it ends

options.label: Nothing; it simply ends
options.clausePhrase: No report is required before the date stated in this Act

options.label: A report to the legislature beforehand
options.clausePhrase: The administering agency shall report to the legislature, not later than one year before the date stated in this Act, on what has been done under the authority this Act ends

options.label: A report, and a hearing on it
options.clausePhrase: The administering agency shall report to the legislature, not later than one year before the date stated in this Act, on what has been done under the authority this Act ends, and the report shall be taken up in a public hearing

evidence.note: An authored review requirement.

rendering.text: This Act applies to {{authority:citationLabel}} and to {{authority:programLabel}} established under it. Nothing in this Act affects an obligation lawfully entered into before the date stated in Section 2.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone {{authority:citationLabel}} reaches

requiredAuthority.message: A sunset reached its authority clause without an authority.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone who would otherwise have applied after that date

clauses.textWhenNoEndDate: {{authority:citationLabel}} shall expire on a date to be fixed by the legislature.

rendering.text: The Act named in Section 1 shall have no further effect after {{date:endsOn}}. No award may be made under it after that date.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: everyone who would otherwise have applied after that date

authorityFallback.textWhenNoEndDate: The Act named in Section 1 shall expire on a date to be fixed by the legislature.

rendering.text: {{choice:pre-sunset-review}}.

amendmentInvitation.heading: Wind-down for applications already filed
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: applicants whose applications are pending on the date
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the towns that applied and were still waiting
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: An application filed in good faith two years ago should not be extinguished by a date, and the towns still in the queue are the ones with the least staff to reapply.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It asks for a saving clause, not for money, and nothing in the world says it was granted.

amendmentInvitation.text: Notwithstanding the expiration required by this Act, an application filed before the date stated in Section 2 shall be determined under the authority as it stood on that date.

variants.label: Replacement expiration date
variants.synopsis: Sets a replacement expiration date and states the reporting conditions. It does not assume the previous expiration is known.
declaredLimits: It sets a date for the authority to end. It appropriates nothing.
It does not change who qualifies or what the program may do.

parameters.label: Years from filing to the proposed expiration

evidence.note: An authored replacement expiration measured from this draft’s filing date, not an addition to an unknown earlier date.

options.label: A finding that it did what it was for
options.clausePhrase: The continued authority under this Act ceases unless the legislature finds, in the fourth year after enactment, that the authority has been used for the purposes stated in the Act named in Section 1

rendering.text: This Act replaces the expiration date of {{authority:citationLabel}}. Except for the conditions stated in this Act, it makes no other change to that Act, to {{authority:programLabel}}, or to who may draw on it.

amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: the members who will have to vote on it again
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: The legislature should review the authority before the proposed expiration date.

variants.label: Outright repeal
variants.synopsis: Repeals an existing authority on a stated date, with a saving clause for what was already done under it.
declaredLimits: It repeals an authority. It recovers nothing already provided or spent under it.
It states no amount, and no saving is claimed from it.

parameters.label: Years until the repeal takes effect

amendmentInvitation.heading: Transition for the places that relied on it
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: the communities the repealed program was serving
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the places that built a budget around it
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: This program is a line in somebody's budget, and repealing it in twelve months without a word to them is how a county ends up cutting a service it had no warning about.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It asks for notice rather than for money.

amendmentInvitation.text: The administering agency shall give written notice of the repeal made by this Act to every recipient of an award under the repealed authority not later than six months before its effective date.

families.title: Charges and dedications
families.mechanism: Imposes a charge, or dedicates one already imposed, without authorizing anybody to spend it.

structuralProvenance.establishes: An official estimate distinguishes authorizing legislation from appropriation treatment and states which effects it did not model, rather than presenting one confident total.

intendedOutcome.statement: What the charge actually collects, and from whom.

evidence.note: What a charge raises depends on how many people pay it, which is a behavior rather than a rate.
evidence.unavailableReason: Nothing in this world counts the transactions this charge would apply to, so receipts cannot be estimated.

variants.label: Flat permit fee
variants.synopsis: Imposes a fixed charge on a permit, with a stated exemption and a date it stops.
declaredLimits: It collects. It authorizes nobody to spend what it collects.
What it raises is not stated here, because it depends on how many permits are issued.

evidence.note: An authored fee. No real permit fee schedule is reproduced.

options.label: Nobody is exempt
options.clausePhrase: No exemption from the fee imposed by this Act is allowed

options.label: The smallest projects
options.clausePhrase: A permit for work whose stated value is below the threshold the department publishes is exempt from the fee imposed by this Act

options.label: The smallest projects, and repairs
options.clausePhrase: A permit for work whose stated value is below the threshold the department publishes, and a permit for repair of an existing structure, are exempt from the fee imposed by this Act

evidence.note: An authored exemption.
An authored expiry. A charge with an end date is a different political proposition from a permanent one.

rendering.text: A fee of {{money:fee-amount}} is imposed on each permit issued under the building code of this state. The fee is payable by the applicant at the time the permit is issued.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every applicant for a permit

rendering.text: {{choice:exemption}}.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every applicant the exemption reaches

rendering.text: The fee imposed by this Act shall not be charged on a permit issued after {{date:endsOn}}.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every applicant after that date

clauses.textWhenNoEndDate: The fee imposed by this Act continues until repealed.

amendmentInvitation.heading: Remission for owner-occupied repairs
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: households repairing the house they live in
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the older neighborhoods where the roofs are going
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: A flat fee is the same number for a subdivision and for somebody replacing a roof they live under, and it is the second one who notices it.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It narrows who pays rather than asking for money.

amendmentInvitation.text: The fee imposed by this Act shall be remitted on a permit for repair of a dwelling occupied by its owner, on application to the department.

variants.label: Dedicated surcharge
variants.synopsis: Imposes a surcharge and dedicates every dollar of it to one fund, without authorizing that fund to spend.
declaredLimits: Dedicating money to a fund is not appropriating it out of that fund. Nobody may spend it until a separate Act says so.
It states a rate, not a total. What it raises is not known here.

evidence.note: An authored surcharge. No real rate is reproduced.
An authored dedication share. A partial dedication is a real legislative choice and is offered as one.
An authored expiry.

rendering.text: A surcharge of {{money:surcharge-amount}} is imposed on each vehicle registration renewal issued in this state, and is collected with the renewal fee.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every person renewing a registration

rendering.text: {{integer:dedication-share}} per cent of the surcharge collected under this Act shall be deposited in the road maintenance fund and the remainder in the general fund. Nothing in this Act authorizes any amount to be spent from either.

rendering.text: The whole of the surcharge collected under this Act shall be deposited in the road maintenance fund. No part of it may be used for any other purpose, and nothing in this Act authorizes any amount to be spent from that fund.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: the fund named in this section

clauses.heading: Expiration

rendering.text: The surcharge imposed by this Act shall not be collected on a renewal issued after {{date:endsOn}}.

beneficiary.appliesToLabel: every person renewing after that date

clauses.textWhenNoEndDate: The surcharge imposed by this Act continues until repealed.

amendmentInvitation.heading: Return of a share to the counties that raised it
amendmentInvitation.beneficiaryLabel: counties whose registrations raise more than they get back
amendmentInvitation.placeLabel: the counties with the long distances and the short budgets
amendmentInvitation.statedGround: Every registration in the county pays this, and the fund it goes to has not paved a mile out there in nine years.

evidence.note: An authored request from a fictional member. It redirects a share rather than raising the rate.

amendmentInvitation.text: One fifth of the surcharge collected in a county shall be returned to that county for road maintenance, and the department shall publish annually what each county paid and what it received.
